title: Kth Smallest Amount With Single Denomination Combination
summary: Given an integer array of coin denominations and an integer k, return the k-th smallest amount that can be formed using any number of coins of the same denomination, but not combining different denominations.
statement: Given an integer array of coin denominations and an integer k, return the k-th smallest amount that can be formed using any number of coins of the same denomination, but not combining different denominations.
constraints: coins contains distinct positive denominations and k is positive.
An amount qualifies when it is a positive multiple of at least one denomination; different denominations are never mixed in one construction.
Sort distinct qualifying amounts and return the k-th smallest.
hints: The count of amounts at most x divisible by any coin is a union size computed by inclusion-exclusion over subset LCMs.
Binary-search the smallest x whose union count reaches k.
For each nonempty coin subset add or subtract floor(x/lcm); use that monotone count in lower-bound search.
Inclusion-exclusion counts every qualifying integer once, and the first x with count≥k is exactly the k-th ordered distinct amount.
editorial: Inclusion-exclusion counts every qualifying integer once, and the first x with count≥k is exactly the k-th ordered distinct amount.

tests.explanation: The distinct qualifying amounts begin 3, 6, 9, so the third is nine.
The ordered union is 2,3,4,6,8, so the fifth amount is eight.
